question: Does conditioning party-seat candidate-share response on observed SOURCE victory improve chronological conditional diagnostics, and are conclusions transform-sensitive? Turnover/personal-incumbency adjustment is unsupported.
population: All 382 eligible general National/Labour party-seat pairs from original Stage6, equal record weights; 2 cancellations excluded; Maori coverage only. No identity/status-based selection.
units: C and P are fractions using distinct valid-candidate and valid-party denominators; y=C1-C0, x=P1-P0, W=1 if source party candidate won source seat, otherwise 0. W is not target incumbency or continuity.
fit: Separate party OLS on actual observed x and y only. Exact rational normal-equation elimination from decimal input representations; scaled Gram pivot tolerance 1e-12. At least five rows per free coefficient; sourceWon models require at least five source winners and five source losers. No fitted missingness indicator, interactions, weighting search or alternative status models.
interceptFairness: Every restricted-beta model estimates its own intercept/status nuisance terms on exactly the same permitted training records. Do not compare a fitted-intercept improvement as if it isolated beta.
chronology: Holdouts 2011/2017/2023; train only rows with targetYear < holdout sourceYear. 2011 parameter-free beta0/beta1 only; fitted models explicitly abstain. All full-sample fits descriptive only; never used for holdout prediction.
transformRule: Keep fitted alpha/beta/gamma fixed across modes; substitute Stage5 predicted target party shares only at prediction. National support is observed target conditioning information, not forecast. No transformation refitting or choosing best holdout transform.
bounds: Consume Stage5 lower/upper bounds; affine propagation accounts for beta sign. Singleton intervals support exact point metrics; nondegenerate inputs yield conservative MAE/RMSE/bias enclosures, no midpoint. Observed structural training inputs must be exact; otherwise abstain rather than invent latent data. Never combine marginal extrema into joint realizations.
metrics: Equal record MAE/RMSE/signed bias pp on identical party/holdout/mode samples, with IDs, n, abstentions, outside-[0,1] predictions and source-victory strata. Aggregate trained 2017/2023 holdouts by record count, report each fold and aggregate; no election-iid significance. No vote weighting sensitivity.
materiality: 0.25 pp aggregate MAE gain is indicative only, not significance. Stable means both trained holdouts show positive MAE gain in every input mode; also report RMSE/bias and worst-fold regressions. Material transform sensitivity means range of aggregate MAE gains >=0.25 pp or gain sign reverses. Record disagreement and stop without tuning.
statusEvidence: Inherited Stage8/9/10 and Stage13 evidence remains audit-only. No broad prospective relation/tenure cohort; no turnover or target-incumbency gamma fitted. W is directly observed source-election victory. Source victory can proxy baseline level, selection and regression-to-mean; its coefficient is not causal incumbency.
counterfactual: Holding evidence fixed, later winner flags/candidate outcomes cannot affect inventory/predictor construction. Held-out candidate shares may score only. Source election outcomes legitimately determine C0 and W; earlier training outcomes legitimately determine fitted coefficients. Target party votes are allowed conditional inputs.
stage15: Use same conditional observed-local-party mode for overlap accounting only. Stage15 has no point predictions, so no point ranking. No interval-vs-point coverage contest implying relative predictive quality.
stopping: If conditioning fails evidence/rank/training gates, abstain. Preserve out-of-range predictions without clipping; do not normalize two parties into a whole ballot model. No source acquisition, effect stacking, as-of forecast, target-boundary baseline, integration or later model selection.
